scheme_name: Advanced Animal Breeding Scheme (Supply of Breedable Pedigree Murrah Bull on Subsidy)
description:
The Advanced Animal Breeding Scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance the productivity of the dairy sector through the supply of breedable pedigree Murrah bulls on subsidy. 

This scheme was officially launched in 2014 under the National Programme for Dairy Development. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to improve the genetic quality of livestock in India. 

The scheme aims to increase milk production by enhancing the breeding of high-yielding dairy animals. 

The target is to provide at least 10,000 pedigree Murrah bulls annually to farmers across various states. 

The scheme also seeks to promote the use of artificial insemination techniques among dairy farmers. 

By improving the genetic quality of dairy cattle, the scheme aims to increase the average milk yield per animal. 

The average milk yield of a Murrah bull can reach up to 20 liters per day. 

This is significantly higher than the average yield of local breeds, which can be as low as 5 to 7 liters per day. 

The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance to farmers for purchasing pedigree bulls. 

Farmers can receive a subsidy of up to 50 percent of the cost of the bull. 

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 25,000 per bull. 

This means that if a pedigree Murrah bull costs INR 50,000, the farmer would only need to pay INR 25,000 after the subsidy. 

The scheme also provides training and support to farmers on the management of these bulls. 

Farmers are educated about the benefits of using high-quality bulls for breeding purposes. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a registered dairy farmer. 

Farmers must also be part of a cooperative society or a self-help group. 

There are no specific age limits for applicants. 

However, farmers must demonstrate a commitment to dairy farming. 

An income criterion is not explicitly mentioned in the scheme guidelines. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, farmers must approach their local animal husbandry department. 

They need to fill out an application form provided by the department. 

The application form requires details such as the farmer's name, address, and details of the cooperative society or self-help group. 

Farmers must also provide proof of their dairy farming activities. 

This may include documents such as a dairy farming license or registration certificate. 

After submission, the application will be reviewed by the local animal husbandry officials. 

Once approved, the farmer will receive a sanction order for the subsidy. 

The farmer can then proceed to purchase the pedigree Murrah bull from an authorized supplier. 

The disbursement of the subsidy amount is typically made directly to the supplier. 

Farmers are encouraged to keep records of their purchases and breeding activities. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the department can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is operational in several states across India. 

States such as Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan have been particularly active in implementing this scheme. 

The timeline for the disbursement of subsidies is generally within 30 days of the purchase of the bull. 

Farmers are advised to complete their applications and purchases promptly to avoid delays. 

The scheme has been positively received by the dairy farming community. 

It has contributed to an increase in the population of high-yielding dairy animals. 

The overall impact on milk production in the states where the scheme is implemented has been significant. 

According to reports, milk production in these states has increased by approximately 10 to 15 percent since the scheme's launch. 

The scheme also aims to reduce the dependency on low-yielding local breeds. 

By promoting pedigree bulls, the government aims to enhance the overall quality of milk produced in India. 

This is crucial as India is the largest producer of milk in the world, contributing to over 22 percent of global milk production. 

The Advanced Animal Breeding Scheme is part of a broader strategy to modernize the dairy sector in India. 

It aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme also contributes to food security and nutritional enhancement for the population. 

By improving milk production, the scheme supports the livelihoods of millions of dairy farmers. 

The government continuously monitors the implementation of the scheme to ensure its effectiveness. 

Feedback from farmers is collected to make necessary adjustments to the program. 

The scheme has also been linked with other initiatives such as the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi. 

This linkage provides additional financial support to farmers engaged in dairy farming. 

Overall, the Advanced Animal Breeding Scheme represents a significant effort by the Indian government to enhance the dairy sector. 

It provides concrete benefits to farmers while aiming for long-term improvements in livestock quality and productivity. 

The focus on pedigree Murrah bulls is a strategic choice given their proven track record in high milk yield. 

As the scheme continues to evolve, it is expected to play a crucial role in shaping the future of dairy farming in India. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to improve their dairy operations. 

The government remains committed to supporting the dairy sector through various welfare schemes. 

This commitment is reflected in the resources allocated for the implementation of the Advanced Animal Breeding Scheme. 

With ongoing support and improvements, the scheme is poised to have a lasting impact on the dairy industry in India.
